finding.claim: purge handler calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards its bool return, so the admin check never denies the request and purgeAll() runs for any user reaching the route.
finding.source: HTTP request to purge handler; user from context via userFrom (handlers.go:25)
finding.guards_checked: checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) returns bool but is not used as a guard; contrast mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22) used correctly by rotateKeys at handlers.go:33-35. Route registration and auth middleware are not in this repo, so reachability is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: none. checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) returns a bool, and the purge handler discards it at handlers.go:26 as a bare statement. purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs unconditionally. mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22) is the guard that rotateKeys uses correctly at handlers.go:33-35, and purge does not use it. Route registration and auth middleware are not in this repo.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: userFrom at handlers.go:25 reads the user, checkPerm's bool at handlers.go:26 is discarded, and purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any caller. The only open question is whether route middleware restricts the route to admins, which is not in this repo; the handler itself has no admin enforcement, so the defect stands at the code level.
